recent_articles.title: Manipur DGP moved to Cabinet Secretariat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajiv Singh**, a 1993 batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of Tripura cadre, has been appointed Secretary (Security) in the **Cabinet Secretariat**.  He was appointed as Manipur's police chief in June 2023 following ethnic violence between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo people. The **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet** approved his appointment on Thursday, May 21, 2026. Singh oversaw the recovery of over 4,500 weapons looted from police armouries after the May 2023 violence and led efforts to arrest around 1,000 extortionists during Manipur's state of President's Rule.

recent_articles.title: SC asks Centre to consider States’ pleas for funds for CCTVs in police stations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** urged the **Union government** to fully implement the Assistance to States and Union Territories for Modernisation of Police (ASUMP) scheme, which provides funds for installing CCTV cameras in police stations and a centralized monitoring dashboard. The court expressed concerns over non-functional CCTV cameras in Udaipur police stations and directed the Centre to consider requests from states for funding.  The ASUMP scheme has been extended until September 30, 2026, with most states initiating steps towards compliance. However, Jharkhand was criticized for not installing any CCTV cameras, despite receiving funds under the scheme. The court also cautioned against releasing funds without due diligence to prevent misappropriation.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Tripura pharmacists to join strike on May 20 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists** is calling for a strike on May 20th, affecting health services in **Tripura**. The strike demands the cessation of online medicine sales, corporate-run industry deep discounts, and the halt of spurious medication sales.  **The Tripura Chemists and Druggists Association**, affiliated with the national body, will join the strike, resulting in approximately 3,000 pharmacies remaining closed. **The State Health and Family Welfare Department** and **the State Drug Control Authority** are reportedly taking steps to mitigate the impact of the strike.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: BJP’s victory in Bengal will plug a big hole in national security, says Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, stated that the BJP's victory in West Bengal was significant for national security, as it plugs a major hole and will make infiltration and cattle smuggling impossible. He emphasized that this victory signifies ideological continuity for the party, marking its presence across all states from Gangotri to Gangasagar.  **Shah** also highlighted the importance of the victory in light of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 150th birth anniversary and thanked voters for their support. The BJP Legislature Party leader, **Suvendu Adhikari**, will be sworn in as the Chief Minister on May 9th.

recent_articles.title: PM Modi on West Bengal election result: ‘Lotus’ is blooming from Gangotri to Gangasagar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** praised the outcomes of the elections in four States and a Union Territory as a triumph of democracy and the Constitution, attributing the BJP's success to voters seeking stability and development amidst global turmoil. He highlighted women's crucial role in building a developed India, accusing the Congress and Samajwadi Party of blocking women's reservation in the Lok Sabha.  **Modi** expressed confidence that the BJP-led NDA would continue its efforts to serve people and work ceaselessly for a developed India.

recent_articles.title: Tripura BJP celebrates win in Assembly bye-election - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The BJP** celebrated a victory in the Dharmanagar assembly by-election in Tripura, with candidate Jahar Chakraborti securing over 18,000 votes.  **Dr. Manik Saha**, **Chief Minister of Tripura**, and other party leaders participated in a victory procession in Agartala. The saffron party's win follows victories in West Bengal and Assam.

recent_articles.title: India loses its last left-wing government after five decades | Politics News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: India's left-wing parties have lost their grip on power, with the **United Democratic Front** winning the Kerala state elections. This marks the first time in over half a century that no Indian state is ruled by the left. The decline of the left's influence is attributed to factors such as its inability to address issues like caste and gender inequality and its perceived lack of relevance in the face of changing economic realities. Experts suggest that while the left may not be in power, it remains an important opposition force capable of influencing policy debates.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal: Modi's BJP conquers one of India's toughest political frontiers
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a decisive victory in West Bengal, marking a significant breakthrough for **Narendra Modi** and his 12-year reign.  This unexpected outcome comes after years of the party's struggle to gain traction in the state, which has traditionally been dominated by the Trinamool Congress (TMC). The BJP's success is attributed to a combination of factors, including its aggressive welfare pitch, sharpened Hindu consolidation efforts, and a focus on alleged corruption within the TMC. This victory will likely have far-reaching implications for the BJP's future trajectory, potentially solidifying **Amit Shah**'s position as Modi's successor.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 results: Counting of votes begins across five States - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Counting of votes for the Assembly elections in five states, including Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and West Bengal, is underway.  **Election Commission of India (ECI)** officials are overseeing the process at designated counting centers across the country. Early trends suggest a tight race in several constituencies with the **DMK** seeking to retain power in Tamil Nadu, while the **AIADMK** and independent candidates like Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam are vying for victory. In Kerala, the ruling Left Democratic Front faces competition from the Opposition United Democratic Front (UDF) and Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).  Security arrangements have been tightened across all states to ensure a smooth and peaceful counting process.

recent_articles.title: Incessant rain damages over 6,000 hectares of agricultural land in Tripura - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ratan Lal Nath**, **Tripura's Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare**, confirmed the severe impact of heavy rainfall on agriculture and horticulture in the state.  Rainfall between April 27th and 29th reached an average of 133.9 mm, with some areas experiencing over 283 mm. Preliminary assessments reveal approximately 6,105 hectares of farmland have been affected, leading to a potential production loss of 21,635 metric tonnes with an estimated value of ₹59.17 crore. The **Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Department** has prepared a disaster management plan, including the deployment of Quick Response Teams for immediate action and field officials on alert for damage assessment.

recent_articles.title: Why is India turning to crocodiles and snakes to ‘fence’ Bangladesh border? | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Indian** Border Security Force (BSF) is exploring the use of apex predators like crocodiles and venomous snakes to deter undocumented migration along its border with **Bangladesh**.  This controversial plan, aimed at addressing challenging terrain that makes traditional fencing difficult, has raised concerns from human rights activists and wildlife conservationists. The BSF's directive to explore this option comes despite the fact that these animals are not native to the region and could pose a threat to local ecosystems and communities. Critics argue that deploying such measures is inhumane and ineffective, highlighting the government's use of fear tactics against undocumented migrants. This approach has been compared to similar controversial strategies employed in the United States, including proposals for using alligators or snakes to deter migrants.

recent_articles.title: ₹127.69 crore has been restored to victims of Rose Valley Group scam: ED - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Enforcement Directorate (ED)** and the **Asset Disposal Committee (ADC)** have continued efforts to restore funds to victims of the Rose Valley Group scam.  They have completed 16 phases of disbursements, releasing ₹127.69 crore to over 1.73 lakh people. The group defrauded investors of approximately ₹17,520 crore, with ₹6,666 crore still outstanding. **The ED** has attached or seized assets worth ₹1,568 crore in multiple states and recently handed over a demand draft for ₹517.54 crore to the ADC. The agencies are also automating claims and disbursement processes using AI technology and collaborating with government companies to revamp the refund portal.

recent_articles.title: Karbi Anglong lynching: Assam court convicts 20 for murder of Abhijeet and Nilotpal
recent_articles.rephrased_article: In 2018, **Abhijeet Nath** and **Nilotpal Das**, two men from Guwahati, were killed in Karbi Anglong, Assam, after being accused of being child kidnappers by a mob. A court recently convicted 20 people for murder and unlawful assembly while acquitting 25 others due to lack of evidence. The families of the victims expressed dissatisfaction with the verdict, stating they are considering legal options. This case highlights the dangers of misinformation spreading online, particularly through WhatsApp, which fueled suspicion and led to mob violence across India.  The incident also spurred a national conversation about how to curb the spread of false information and hold those responsible accountable.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Government** celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.
